text:
Who cries that eleven is not twelve!

As if they had been bid up, they confront each other

two by two, the eleven times.


Brutal headbutt. Crowns appear

to listen,

but without crossing the eternal

three hundred sixty degrees, they appear

and explore in vain where both hands

hide the other bridge that is born to them

between truths and liturgical jokes.


The frontier returns to test

the two stones that cannot manage to occupy

one same lodging at one same time.

The frontier, the wandering baton, which remains

unchanged, equal, only

more itself at each high sprain.


You see what is without being able to be denied,

you see what we have to endure,

despite ourselves.

How much is oiled in elbows

that reach all the way to the mouth!

translation.title: Trilce: Poem LIII - Who Cries That Eleven Is Not Twelve
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the clock-number dispute, frontier, baton, and body-mechanics of endurance.
